newsitem.title: USA: FTC ready to talk with Staples, Office Depot again.
newsitem.headline: FTC ready to talk with Staples, Office Depot again.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission announced Wednesday it was willing to speak with Office Depot, OfficeMax and Staples about a merger and divestiture deal.
"If they have something serious to talk about we will talk," a spokeswoman for the FTC said shortly after the companies announced a complicated deal to divest stores.
Under a three-way agreement negotiated by the CEOs of the three chains, 28 Office Depot stores and 35 Staples will be sold to OfficeMax, OfficeMax CEO Michael Feuer told Reuters.
The sale is subject to government approval and all sides hope it will clear the way for a Staples-Office Depot merger.
On Monday the FTC voted to go to court to halt the merger of Office Depot and Staples because the companies were unable to divest stores to OfficeMax.
The FTC had planned to go to court as soon as a critical deadline expired Thursday. Staples is operating under a law that bars it from merging before that deadline was reached.
Staples has now told the government it will extend the deadline until Monday, precluding any government action until at least then.
